rationale: This is a free ad-funded service, not a digital-goods storefront, and it states plainly that users retain ownership of their content while granting a broad usage license; the deception here lies less in disguised 'purchases' and more in expansive, non-negotiable rights grants over user content and feedback, and vague, ad-driven data use. Termination and dispute clauses are relatively consumer-protective (EU-influenced good-cause/cure requirements, no forced arbitration), but the feedback and content-license clauses are broad and one-sided.
evidence_quotes: You own the content you create and share on Facebook... nothing in these Terms takes away the rights you have to your own content
